question.text: Conditions precedent in an investment agreement are:

answer.text: Conditions that must be fulfilled after the investment is completed
Conditions that must be satisfied before the investment can close
Conditions that only apply to the fund manager
Optional suggestions for improving the investee company

explanation.text: The Logic: The term sheet sets out conditions precedent to the investment, and due diligence carried out before firming up the investment can influence the final deal terms. These conditions therefore have to be met before the investment can close. The Trap: Option A reverses the timing — CPs are pre-closing requirements, not post-investment obligations. Option C is wrong because the conditions are part of the broader investment agreement, not limited to the manager. Option D mischaracterises them as optional, whereas they are binding requirements. Note: The detailed catalogue of CPs (regulatory approvals, no MAC, walk-away rights, etc.) depends on the specific transaction and is not exhaustively defined in the workbook.
